The deliverable correctly calculates the long-stop date as 7 July 2027 (90 days after 8 April 2027), identifies the 14-day gap with the expected regulatory clearance date of 21 July 2027, and recommends extending the long-stop date.

The deliverable correctly states that General Warranty claims must be notified by 28 May 2028 (12 months from Closing on 28 May 2027) and Fundamental Warranty claims by 28 May 2030 (36 months from Closing).

The deliverable explains the spectrum of interpretations for 'material adverse effect' (narrow interpretation requiring significant long-term impact versus broad interpretation including short-term effects) and analyzes what each means for the Buyer's walk-away right under Clause 4.3(b).

Foxley Foods Ltd (the Buyer) is acquiring the entire issued share capital of Larkspur Holdings Ltd (the Company) from Rothley Medical Ltd (the Seller). London banking days (excl. weekends/public holidays)
2. English court days
3. Calendar days | Payment timing ambiguity; potential breach disputes | High - Payment deadline uncertainty | "a day (other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday) on which banks are open for general business in London" | | **Encumbrances** (Clause 4.2) | 1. Security interests only
2. All third-party rights/claims
3. Legal and equitable interests | Title transfer completeness; hidden liabilities | Medium - Unclear what transfers "free from" | "any mortgage, charge, pledge, lien, option, restriction, right of pre-emption, right of first refusal or other third party right or interest" | **Legal Consequence:** Ambiguity in calculating payment notification deadlines could lead to disputes over timely payment, potentially constituting a breach. Material Adverse Change (MAC) Clause Analysis **Clause Reference:** Clause 1.1 (Interpretation) and Clause 4.3(b) (Conditions) **Risk Rating:** Medium **Direct Quote:** ""Material Adverse Change" means any event, change or effect which has a material adverse effect on the business, assets, financial condition or results of operations of the Company taken as a whole, excluding any effect to the extent resulting from: (a) changes in general economic, business or political conditions; (b) changes affecting the food production industry generally; or (c) pandemics, provided that such exclusions shall not apply to the extent that the Company is disproportionately affected relative to other participants in its industry."
